No storm in sight this week

No. As of the Nov 2, 2026 evening snapshot, there are zero active weather alerts across all eight states we track (National Weather Service alerts). The forecast for our Central PA hubs is dry and warming through Nov 4, 2026.

What the forecast shows

  • No rain or snow. Precipitation is 0.0 inches at every hub shown, Nov 2 to Nov 4, 2026. Chance of rain stays at 8% or lower (Open-Meteo 7-day forecast).
  • Warm for November. Highs climb from about 65–67°F on Nov 2 to about 71–73°F on Nov 4, 2026.
  • Windier on Wednesday. Gusts rise on Nov 4, 2026, peaking at 28 mph in York and 27.5 mph in Lancaster.
  • Possible morning fog. Some hubs show weather code 45 on Nov 3–4, 2026. On the standard forecast code scale, that is fog.

What it means for calls

No weather driver is active, so the demand model leaves call volume at the seasonal baseline (est.) (Punctual Pros demand model). The model's heating multipliers are still assumptions, not fitted values. Our own booked-call history would show how a warm early-November week actually plays out.

A quiet week lets dispatch shift techs from emergency calls to maintenance and replacement work, which supports margin in a portfolio company where franchise fees take about 7.2–7.5% of revenue (est.) (Punctual Pros public filings).

Next actions

  1. Pull the full ten-hub forecast through Nov 8, 2026, including the NJ hubs.
  2. Brief dispatch on Wednesday gusts near 28 mph for roof and attic work in York and Lancaster.
  3. Use the quiet window to book heating tune-ups, starting with oil and propane households.
  4. Compare this week's booked calls against the model's baseline to help calibrate the heating multipliers.
